report:
Assessed the full identity_minting claim, ten ordinary implementation entries across eight files, and the sole associated TODO test. Requirements are one owning minting query per generic parameter or associated item, dependent queries reusing that identity rather than independently constructing identities from names/positions, and the linked qualification that GenericParam is its own identity family rather than an erased Symbol (fields and locals have owner-scoped identities). Captured checking.sage and the architectural-foundations RFD to inspect that qualification.

Implementation inspection: cst/generics.rs CheckGenerics creates AstGenericParam handles with the owning Symbol and parameter index, then places those same handles in the returned generic slice and resolver. generic_param.rs defines tracked AstGenericParam identity with parent/kind/name/index and tracked mutable span; its unified enum carries existing local/external/alpha-equivalence handles. LocalStructSym::sig, LocalEnumSym::sig, LocalImplSym::sig, LocalTraitSym::sig, and LocalFnSym::sig are tracked owner queries invoking this minting helper. Trait signature alone creates its implicit Self parameter with its own parent and sentinel index. Method signature open_owner copies the owner's binder and Self type, registers existing parameters, and appends only newly declared method parameters. Struct fields reopen sig().iter_symbols(); enum field types are checked under the same signature binder. Trait/impl item enumeration passes the owner's signature parameters into lower_items. Function body first obtains its signature, registers its existing binder symbols, and imports its types and owner Self rather than calling CheckGenerics. Captured BinderExt confirms iter_symbols copies handles; captured ribs confirms add_generic_params stores Resolution::Param(gp) without construction; captured import_fn_sig copies semantic values into body storage without minting parameters.

Both associated.rs entries are tracked keyed owner queries (trait and impl). lower_items and detail-free membership enumeration route through those same queries with kind/name/occurrence keys. Only the keyed query invokes lower_item, which creates a function, type-alias, or constant symbol with its associated owner and current syntax/span. A key locates source inside the owning query; it is not a separately minted identity in each consumer. Associated item definitions and membership return those existing handles. The associated-type-value path in impls.rs also obtains the item through the same keyed owner query and reuses owner generics. Source movement affects tracked spans rather than creating a separate body/signature identity. This inspection supports the ordinary implementation associations, while it is not a substitute for persistent-database assertions.

Test adequacy remains explicitly deferred. The only associated function is todo::checking_identity_minting; it contains no behavioral assertions and is not counted as successful verification. Its comment specifically calls for cross-query and persistent-edit comparisons of owner, generic-parameter, Self and associated-item identities across signatures, field/member detail and bodies, including shadowed equal names. This is an honest outstanding verification matrix: completing it requires source-backed fixtures that observe actual identities from these products in one database, preserve the database across edits, and compare identities for repeated requests and shadowed declarations. The existing TODO covers the full claim's unresolved test evidence; no ordinary test or passing placeholder is asserted here. No new suspected behavioral defect was identified in the inspected minting/reopening paths.

Commands: fresh cargo meta review start with coordinator instructions; review read captures for relevant design/RFD, Binder implementation, resolver ribs and signature import; source and complete associated-test inspection. An attempted ribs line range exceeded the file and was rejected; a subsequent successful whole-file read captured it. No tests or build were run by this reviewer; centrally reported results remain separate. No source edits. No requested changes beyond the explicitly retained existing TODO verification work.
